name: AI for Daily Life
objectives: Using a free AI assistant, ask for easy meal ideas that say how many people you cook for, your time, what you like and what to avoid, getting three ideas that fit your needs and your doctor's advice
Given a few meal ideas, get one shopping list grouped by store section, leaving off what you already have, saved in Notes, printed or written down
Using your phone's voice assistant, set a reminder or timer by speaking, with a day and time, and check on the screen that it is set
Given a real appointment, add it to your phone's calendar with an alert, with the right name, date, time and an alert before it
Given a confusing letter from an insurer, utility or office, get it explained in plain words with all private details left out, and confirm what to do by calling the number printed on the letter

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Planning simple meals with AI
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Ask an AI assistant for a few easy meal ideas that fit your needs.
This lesson builds toward: Using a free AI assistant, you will ask for easy meal ideas that say how many people you cook for, your time, what you like and what to avoid, getting three ideas that fit your needs and your doctor's advice.
Deciding what to cook every day can be tiring, especially when cooking for one or two. An AI assistant can suggest ideas in seconds.
Tell it what you like, how many people you cook for, how much time and effort you want to spend, and anything you must avoid. For example: "I cook for one. Suggest three easy dinners that take under 30 minutes, use a few ingredients, and are low in salt."
If your doctor has given you a special diet, follow your doctor's advice. The assistant can give ideas, but it does not know your health.
Step by step:
- Open your AI assistant.
- Say how many people you cook for.
- Say how much time you have and what you like.
- Say anything to avoid, such as too much salt or sugar.
- Ask for three ideas.
Words to know:
- Ingredient: one of the foods that go into a recipe.
Try it now: Ask an AI assistant for three easy dinners for the coming week that fit how you like to eat. Write down the three you like best.
You can now ask an AI assistant for meal ideas that fit your needs.

check.q: Who decides your special diet if you have one?
check.why: The assistant gives ideas but does not know your health; follow your doctor's advice.

check.q: You cook for two and have little energy in the evening. What do you add to your meal request?
options: "Make it quick and easy, for two people."
check.why: Saying how many people and how much time and effort you want gets ideas that fit.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Turning meals into a shopping list
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Get one tidy shopping list for several meals.
This lesson builds toward: Given a few meal ideas, you will get one shopping list grouped by store section, leaving off what you already have, saved in Notes, printed or written down.
Once you have meal ideas, ask the assistant to make one shopping list for all of them. This saves you from writing out each recipe.
Ask it to group the list by the parts of the store, such as fruit and vegetables, dairy and canned goods, so you walk through the store once. Then tell it what you already have at home so it leaves those off.
You can print the list, copy it into your phone's Notes app, or simply write it on paper. Use whatever is easiest for you.
Step by step:
- Ask: "Make one shopping list for these three dinners."
- Ask it to group the list by store section.
- Tell it what you already have.
- Copy the list into Notes, print it, or write it down.
Words to know:
- Notes app: an app on your phone for writing and saving short notes and lists.
Try it now: Ask the assistant for one shopping list for your three dinners, grouped by store section. Tell it two things you already have, and keep the final list.
You can now turn meal ideas into one shopping list that fits your kitchen.

check.q: What does grouping a list by store section mean?
options: Sorting items from cheapest to most costly
Putting items together by where they are, such as dairy or canned goods
check.why: Grouping by section lets you walk through the store once.

check.q: You already have rice and eggs at home. What do you tell the assistant?
options: To add more rice and eggs
To make a new meal plan
That you already have rice and eggs, so it leaves them off
check.why: Telling it what you have keeps those items off the list.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Using your phone's voice assistant for reminders
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Set a reminder or timer by speaking to your phone.
This lesson builds toward: Using your phone's voice assistant, you will set a reminder or timer by speaking, with a day and time, and check on the screen that it is set.
Most phones have a voice assistant built in: Siri on iPhone, and Google Assistant or Gemini on many Android phones. You speak, and the phone does a simple job, such as setting a reminder, a timer or an alarm.
To start it, you can usually say "Hey Siri" or "Hey Google", or press and hold the side or home button. If it is not set up, ask a family member to help you turn it on in Settings.
Then speak clearly: "Remind me to go grocery shopping on Thursday at 10 am." "Set a timer for 20 minutes." "Remind me to call Ruth tomorrow at 5 pm." The phone will tell you or show you that it is set.
Step by step:
- Say "Hey Siri" or "Hey Google", or press and hold the side or home button.
- Wait for the sound or the light on screen.
- Say what you want, with the day and time.
- Check the screen to see that it is set.
Words to know:
- Voice assistant: a helper built into your phone that does simple jobs when you speak to it.
- Reminder: a message your phone shows you at a time you choose.
Try it now: Use your phone's voice assistant to set a reminder to go grocery shopping on a day and time that works for you. Check that it appears on the screen.
You can now set a reminder or timer by speaking to your phone.

check.q: What is a voice assistant on a phone?
options: A person who calls you back
A built-in helper you speak to, like Siri or Google Assistant
check.why: Siri and Google Assistant do simple jobs, like reminders and timers, when you speak.

check.q: You want to remember to call your sister tomorrow evening. What do you say?
options: "Remind me to call my sister tomorrow at 6 pm."
check.why: A clear request with the task, day and time sets a useful reminder.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Adding appointments to your phone's calendar
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Add a doctor's appointment to your phone's calendar with an alert.
This lesson builds toward: Given a real appointment, you will add it to your phone's calendar with an alert, with the right name, date, time and an alert before it.
Your phone has a Calendar app that can hold all your appointments and warn you before each one. This is handy for doctor's visits, haircuts and family birthdays.
The easiest way is to ask your voice assistant: "Add an appointment with Dr. Lee on May 12 at 2 pm." You can also open the Calendar app, tap the plus sign (+), type the name, choose the date and time, and tap Add or Save.
Set an alert so the phone reminds you ahead of time, such as one day before and one hour before. Look for a choice called Alert or Notification when you add the event.
Step by step:
- Open the Calendar app, or ask your voice assistant.
- Tap the plus sign (+) to add an event.
- Type the name, such as "Dr. Lee checkup".
- Choose the date and the time.
- Choose an alert, such as 1 day before.
- Tap Add or Save.
Words to know:
- Calendar app: the app on your phone that keeps your appointments by date.
- Alert: a sound or message the phone gives you before an appointment.
Try it now: Add one real appointment or family birthday to your phone's calendar with an alert one day before. Check that it shows on the right date.
You can now add an appointment to your phone's calendar and get a reminder before it.

check.q: What does an alert on a calendar appointment do?
options: Makes the phone remind you before the appointment
check.why: An alert warns you ahead of time, such as one day or one hour before.

check.q: You just booked a checkup for next Tuesday. What is the first step to add it in the Calendar app?
options: Write it in a text to yourself
Tap the plus sign (+) to add an event
check.why: Tap the plus sign, then type the name and choose the date, time and an alert.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Getting a confusing letter explained
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Ask an AI assistant to explain a confusing letter in plain words, without sharing private details.
This lesson builds toward: Given a confusing letter from an insurer, utility or office, you will get it explained in plain words with all private details left out, and confirm what to do by calling the number printed on the letter.
Letters from insurance companies, utility companies or offices can be full of hard words. An AI assistant can explain them in plain language.
First, cover or leave out private details: names, account numbers, Medicare or Social Security numbers, and your address. Then type in the confusing part, or describe it, and ask: "Explain this in simple words. What, if anything, do I need to do?"
Some assistants let you take a photo of a page. If you do this, cover the private details before you take the picture. For anything about money, benefits or health, confirm what to do by calling the number printed on the letter itself, or ask a trusted family member.
Step by step:
- Cover or leave out names, numbers and your address.
- Type or describe only the confusing part.
- Ask: "Explain this in simple words. What do I need to do?"
- Confirm by calling the number printed on the letter.
Words to know:
- Plain language: simple, everyday words that are easy to understand.
- Account number: a private number a company uses for your account; never share it with AI.
Try it now: Find a letter or bill with a sentence you do not fully understand. Leave out all private details, type only that sentence into an assistant, and ask it to explain it in simple words.
You can now get a confusing letter explained in plain words while keeping your private details safe.

check.why: Plain language means simple, everyday words that are easy to understand.

check.q: You want to photograph an insurance letter for the AI. What do you do first?
options: Cover your name, address and account numbers
Add your Medicare number so it can check
check.why: Cover private details before you take the picture.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Putting it together: your week, made easier
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use AI and your phone together to plan a week.
This lesson builds toward: Using a free AI assistant, you will ask for easy meal ideas that say how many people you cook for, your time, what you like and what to avoid, getting three ideas that fit your needs and your doctor's advice. Given a few meal ideas, you will get one shopping list grouped by store section, leaving off what you already have, saved in Notes, printed or written down. Using your phone's voice assistant, you will set a reminder or timer by speaking, with a day and time, and check on the screen that it is set.
You now have several small skills: asking for meal ideas, making a list, setting reminders and adding appointments. Used together, they can organize a whole week.
A simple routine: on Sunday, ask the assistant for three dinners and one shopping list. Set a reminder for your shopping day. Look at your calendar to see the week's appointments, and add anything new.
Keep it simple. Use the tools that help you and skip the ones that do not. Paper lists still work well, and asking a family member for help is always fine.
Step by step:
- Ask an AI assistant for three dinners.
- Ask for one shopping list.
- Set a reminder for your shopping day.
- Check your calendar and add new appointments.
Words to know:
- Routine: a set of steps you do the same way each time.
Try it now: Final task: plan three simple dinners for next week with an AI assistant, ask for one shopping list, set a phone reminder for your shopping day, and add one real appointment to your calendar.
You can now use AI and your phone together to plan meals, shop and keep track of appointments.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Meal ideas that fit The request is vague or the meals do not fit your needs. Three dinners that fit how many people, your time, what you like and what to avoid. The meals also follow any diet your doctor gave you. One shopping list No list, or separate lists for each meal. One list for all three dinners, saved in Notes, printed or written down. Grouped by store section, with items you already have left off. Shopping reminder No reminder, or it has no day or time. A reminder set with a day and time, checked on the screen. Set it by speaking to the voice assistant. Appointment in the calendar No appointment, or the date or time is wrong. One real appointment with the right name, date and time. Includes an alert, such as one day before. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: Which tools together can organize your week?
options: Meal ideas, a shopping list, reminders and your calendar
check.why: The small skills from this course work together to plan a whole week.

check.q: It is Sunday. What is a simple first step for planning your week?
options: Ask the assistant for three dinners and one shopping list
check.why: The routine starts with three dinners and one list, then a reminder and a calendar check.
